akhfash:54-54.t: He said: ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ وَٱلنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَاتٍ بِأَمْرِهِ﴾: this is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to His words ﴿خَلَقَ ٱلسَمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ﴾, i.e. "and He created ﴿الشَمْسَ والقَمَرَ﴾".

akhfash:56-56.t:
He said: ﴿إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾. He made ﴿قَرِيب﴾ masculine although it is an adjective (ṣifa) of "الرحمة" (mercy, feminine). This is like the Arabs' saying "رِيحٌ خَريقٌ" (a violent wind), "مِلْحَفَةٌ جَديدٌ" (a new wrap) and "شاةٌ سَدِيسٌ" (a ewe in its sixth year). Or, if you wish, you may say: the explanation of "الرحمة" here is rain and the like; that is why it is made masculine, just as He said ﴿وَإِن كَانَ طَآئِفَةٌ مِّنكُمْ آمَنُواْ﴾ and used the masculine because He meant "people". Or, if you wish, you may treat it like some of the feminine nouns that they make masculine, as in the poet's words [in the mutaqārib metre, and it is the thirty-first poetic witness]:
[فَلا مِزْنَةٌ وَدَقَتْ وَدْقَها] * وَلا أَرْضُ* أَبْقَلَ إِبْقَالها
(No rain-cloud poured down its rain as it did, and no land put forth herbage as it did.)

akhfash:57-57.t:
He said: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُرْسِلُ ٱلرِّيَاحَ بُشْراً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾, because it is the plural of "النَشُور"; you say "رِيحٌ نَشُور" and "رياحٌ نُشُر". Some read "نَشْرا", from "نَشَرها" "نَشْراً" (He spread them out, a spreading).
And He said at the beginning of this sura ﴿كِتَابٌ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ [2] ﴿لِتُنذِرَ بِهِ﴾ [2] ﴿فَلاَ يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِّنْهُ﴾ [2]: this is how it is interpreted, by way of advancing and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr, i.e. inversion of order). There is much like this in the Book of Allah. He said ﴿ٱذْهَب بِّكِتَابِي هَـٰذَا فَأَلْقِهْ إِلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَٱنْظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is ﴿فَٱنْظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾. And in the Book of Allah: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلاَّ رِجَالاً نُّوحِيۤ إِلَيْهِمْ فَٱسْأَلُواْ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنْتُم لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلزُّبُرِ﴾, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلاَّ رِجَالاً نُّوحِيۤ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ ﴿بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلزُّبُرِ﴾ ﴿فَٱسْأَلُواْ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾ ﴿إِن كُنْتُم لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾. And in "Ḥā-Mīm al-Muʾmin": ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرِحُواْ بِمَا عِندَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ﴾, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ ﴿مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ﴾ ﴿فَرِحُواْ بِمَا عِندَهُمْ﴾. Some said that ﴿فَرِحُوا بِما﴾ is ﴿عِنْدَهُم مِنَ الِعلْم﴾, i.e. they had "knowledge" which was in fact ignorance. Advancing and postponing of this kind is frequent in the speech of the Arabs and in poetry. A man writes: "أَمّا بَعْدُ حَفِظَكَ اللهُ وَعافاكَ فإِنّي كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْكَ" (As for what follows — may Allah preserve you and keep you well — I have written to you); his words "فَإِنِّي" are attached to "أَمَّا بَعْدُ" — it is really "أَمَّا بَعْدُ فإِنّي" — and between them, as you see, there is other speech. The poet said [in the kāmil metre, and it is the two hundred and eighth poetic witness]:
خَيْرٌ مِنَ القَوْمِ العُصاةِ أَمِيرَهُم * يا قومُ فاستَحْيُوا النِسَاءُ الجُلَّسُ
(Better than the people who disobey their commander — O people, be ashamed! — are the women who sit at home.)
The meaning is: خيرٌ مِنَ القَوْمِ العصاةِ أميرَهُم النِّساءُ الجُلَّسُ يا قومُ فاسْتَحْيُوا. Another said [in the basīṭ metre, and it is the two hundred and ninth poetic witness]:
الشَّمْشُ طالِعَةٌ لَيْسَتْ بِكاسِفَةٍ * تَبْكِي عليكَ نُجُومَ اللَّيْلِ والقَمَرا
(The sun has risen yet does not eclipse the stars of the night and the moon, weeping for you.)
Its meaning is: the sun has risen and has not eclipsed the stars of the night and the moon, because of its grief over "ʿUmar". That is because whenever the sun rises it eclipses the moon and the stars and leaves them no light.
Among the meanings of the Qur'an is the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلاَ تَنكِحُواْ مَا نَكَحَ آبَاؤُكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾. The meaning is not "marry what has already passed"; that is not permissible in speech. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Do not marry the women your fathers married, for you will be punished for it, except what has already passed, for Allah has remitted it from you." Likewise His words ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُكُمْ﴾, then He said ﴿وَأَن تَجْمَعُواْ بَيْنَ ٱلاخْتَيْنِ إَلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: you will be held to account for that, except what has already passed, for Allah has remitted it from you.
And His words ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِي حَآجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رِبِّهِ﴾, then He said ﴿أَوْ كَٱلَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ﴾: the "kāf" is added in speech, and the meaning is: "Have you not seen the one who disputed with Ibrāhīm about his Lord, or the one who passed by a town?" Its like in the Qur'an is ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ﴾, and the meaning is "There is nothing like Him", because Allah has no like. The poet said [in the rajaz metre, and it is the two hundred and tenth poetic witness]:
* فَصُيِّرُوا مثلَ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُول *
(So they were made like eaten straw.)
The meaning is "they were made like straw", and the kāf is redundant (zāʾida). Another said [rajaz, and it is the two hundred and eleventh poetic witness]:
* وَصَالِباتٍ كَكَما يُؤَثْفِين *
(And firm hearth-stones, as they are set up as trivets.)
One of the two kāfs is redundant.
And His words ﴿بَدَّلْنَاهُمْ جُلُوداً غَيْرَهَا﴾ mean "other than them in being roasted", because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, renews them so that it is a severer punishment for them. They are those very same skins that disobeyed Allah the Exalted, but their being roasted is removed, just as a man says to another: "أنتَ اليومَ غيرُك أمْسِ" (Today you are other than you were yesterday), while he is the very same, except that something has decreased in him or increased. And in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَوْ رُدُّواْ لَعَادُواْ لِمَا نُهُواْ عَنْهُ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾. A questioner may ask: how were they liars when they had not yet returned? They would only be liars if they returned. And you have said that one is not called an unbeliever before he disbelieves, even if it is known that he will be an unbeliever. This may mean that they are the liars after this day, just as a man says "أَنَا قائِمٌ" (I am standing) while he is sitting, meaning "I shall stand". Or He says ﴿إِنَّهم لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ meaning the lying and unbelief with which they arrived at the Resurrection, because those who entered the Fire were liars and unbelievers.
And His words ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ إِلىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ﴾: He says "they look to their provision and what comes to them from Allah", just as a man says: "ما أَنْظُرُ إِلاّ إِلَيك" (I look only to you). If it were the looking of the eye, as some people say, the following verse would have made that clear. Do you not see that He said ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ باسِرةٌ تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِها فَاقِرَةٌ﴾ and did not say "and faces that do not look and do not see"? And His words ﴿تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ﴾: the "supposing" here indicates that the looking there is trust in Allah and good certainty, and does not indicate what they said. How could that be, when Allah says ﴿لاَّ تُدْرِكُهُ ٱلأَبْصَارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ ٱلأَبْصَارَ﴾? [Translator's note: this is the author's own theological position on the vision of Allah, translated as written.] And His words ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ mean: you do not will anything of good unless Allah wills that you will it.
And His words ﴿إِذَآ أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا﴾: this is construed according to the meaning, namely that he does not see it. For when you say "كادَ يفعل" you mean only that he came close to doing it but did not do it; and when you say "لم يكد يفعل", the meaning is that he did not come close to doing it and did not do it — this is the correct sense of the speech, and such is the meaning of this verse. However, the language has also allowed "لَمْ يَكَدْ يَفْعَلُ" in the sense of "he did it after difficulty", but this is not the correct sense of the speech, because when one says "كاد يفعل" he means only "he came close to doing it", and when he says "لم يكد يفعل" he is saying "he did not come close to doing it". However, the language has come as I have explained to you, and that is not according to the correct sense of the word.

akhfash:63-63.t: He said: ﴿أَوَ عَجِبْتُمْ أَن جَآءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾. It is as though it were said: "They did such-and-such and wondered", so He said: "You did such-and-such — and do you wonder (أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ)?" This is the wāw of conjunction, with the interrogative alif prefixed to it.

akhfash:65-65.t:
He said: ﴿وَإِلَىٰ عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُوداً﴾ and ﴿وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَالِحاً﴾. All of this — and Allah knows best — is accusative (manṣūb) by the first statement, i.e. by His words ﴿لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحاً إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ﴾; and likewise ﴿لُوطاً﴾. Some said it means "واذْكُرْ لُوطاً" (and mention Lūṭ). This accusative comes only by one of these two ways, or by the verb having governed something before it, and then a verb falls after it on something connected with it, so a verb is implied for it. So it is only by one of these three, and this is frequent in the Qur'an.
And He said ﴿خَلاَئِفَ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ and He said ﴿خُلَفَآءَ﴾; all are permissible, and it is the plural of "الخليفة".

akhfash:69-69.t: He said: ﴿وَزَادَكُمْ فِي ٱلْخَلْقِ بَسْطَةً﴾, i.e. "انْبِساطاً" (extension). In another place it is ﴿بَسْطَةً فِي ٱلْعِلْمِ وَٱلْجِسْمِ﴾, and it is like the first.

akhfash:73-73.t: He said: ﴿فَذَرُوهَا تَأْكُلْ فِيۤ أَرْضِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: jussive (majzūm) if you make it an apodosis (jawāb), and nominative (marfūʿ) if you mean "فَذَرُوها آكِلَةً" (leave her eating). And He said ﴿وَأْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَأْخُذُواْ بِأَحْسَنِهَا﴾, and He said ﴿قُل لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ يَغْفِرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ﴾ and ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُواْ وَيَلْعَبُواْ﴾: it has become an apodosis in wording, but it is not so in meaning.

akhfash:86-86.t: Then He said: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْعُدُواْ بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ تُوعِدُونَ﴾. You say "هُمْ فِي البَصْرَةِ" and "بِالبَصْرَةِ" (they are in Basra), and "قَعَدْتُ لَهُ في الطَّريق" and "بِالطَّريق" (I lay in wait for him on the road).

akhfash:92-92.t: He said: ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْاْ فِيهَا﴾; it is from "غَنِيتَ" "تَغْنَى" "غِنَى" (to dwell, abide).

akhfash:98-98.t: He said: ﴿أَوَ أَمِنَ أَهْلُ ٱلْقُرَىٰ﴾: this wāw is for conjunction, with the interrogative alif prefixed to it.

akhfash:100-100.t: He said: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لِلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلأَرْضَ مِن بَعْدِ أَهْلِهَآ﴾; he says: "Has it not become clear to them?" Some read ﴿نَهْدِ﴾ with nūn, i.e. "Have We not made clear to them" ﴿أَن لَّوْ نَشَآءُ أَصَبْنَاهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾.

akhfash:101-101.t:
He said: ﴿نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنبَآئِهَا﴾: he made "مِنْ" redundant and meant "قصَصْنا" (We have related), just as you say "هل لكَ في ذا" (Do you have [a need] for this?) and omit "حاجة" (need).
And He said ﴿فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: His words ﴿بما كذبو﴾ — and Allah knows best — mean "بِتَكْذِيبِهِم" (because of their denial). He made — and Allah knows best — ﴿مَا كَذَّبُوا﴾ a noun for the action (i.e. a maṣdar, verbal noun), and the meaning is: "they were not such as to believe because of the denial", i.e. We do not call them believers on account of the denial.

akhfash:105-105.t: He said: ﴿حَقِيقٌ عَلَى أَنْ لاَّ أَقُولَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلاَّ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾, and some read ﴿عَلَى أَنْ لا أَقُولَ﴾. [Translator's note: the two readings appear identically in the source; the variant intended is presumably «عَلَيَّ أَنْ لا أَقُولَ».] The first is the better of the two in our view; he meant: "It is incumbent upon me that I not say." The other means: "I am worthy, upon me, that I not say against Allah", and he means "بِأَنْ لا أقولَ على الله" (that I not say against Allah), just as He said ﴿بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ تُوعِدُونَ﴾ in the sense of "على كُلِّ صِراطٍ تُوعِدُون" (on every path, threatening).

akhfash:111-111.t: He said: ﴿أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ﴾ and He said ﴿تُرْجِي مَن تَشَآءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾, because it is from "أَرْجأْتُ" (I postponed). It has been read ﴿أَرْجِهِ وَأَخاه﴾, lightened without hamza, and that is how we read, and ﴿تُرْجِي مَن تَشَآءُ﴾. It is a dialect in which one says "أَرْجَيْتُ"; and some Arabs say "أَخْطَيْتُ" and "تَوَضَّيْتُ", without hamza.

akhfash:126-126.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا تَنقِمُ مِنَّآ﴾, and some read ﴿وَمَا تَنْقَمُ مِنّا﴾. They are two dialects: "نَقَمَ" "يَنْقِمُ" and "نَقِم" "يَنْقَمُ". And we read with it — i.e. with the first.

akhfash:132-132.t: He said: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِ مِن آيَةٍ﴾, because ﴿مَهْما﴾ is one of the particles of condition (ḥurūf al-mujāzāt), and its apodosis is ﴿فَمَا نَحْنُ﴾.

akhfash:133-133.t:
He said: ﴿ٱلطُّوفَانَ﴾; its singular by analogy (qiyās) is "الطُوفانَة". The poet said [in the ramal metre, and it is the two hundred and twelfth poetic witness]:
* غَيْرَ اَلجِدَّةَ مِنْ آياتِها خُرُقُ الرِّيحِ وَطُوفَانُ المَطَر *
(Its traces' freshness was altered by violent winds and the deluge of rain.)
It is from "طافَ" "يَطُوفُ" (to go round).

akhfash:137-137.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعْرِشُونَ﴾; "يَعْرُشونَ" — two dialects. Likewise ﴿نَبْطِشُ﴾ and "نَبْطُشُ", "يَحْشُرُ" and ﴿يحشِرُ﴾, ﴿يعكُفُ﴾ and ﴿يعكِفُ﴾, ﴿ينفُرُ﴾ and ﴿ينفِرُ﴾.

akhfash:143-143.t:
He said: ﴿جَعَلَهُ دَكّاً﴾, because when He said ﴿جَعَلَه﴾ it was as though He had said "دَكَّهُ" (He levelled it) [so دكّا is a maṣdar]. One also says ﴿دَكّاء﴾; if that is meant, then it has been treated like ﴿وَسْئَلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ﴾ [i.e. with a muḍāf omitted], because one says "نَاقَةٌ دَكّاءُ" (a she-camel whose hump has gone).
And He said ﴿فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ﴾; he says: "His command appeared", like what people say: "بَرَزَ فُلانٌ لفُلانٍ" (So-and-so came out against so-and-so), when it was only his army that came out.
As for His words ﴿رَبِّ أَرِنِيۤ أَنظُرْ إِلَيْكَ﴾, he meant only a knowledge whose like is attained only in the Hereafter, so Allah informed Mūsā that this does not happen in this world. Some read it ﴿دَكّاء﴾, making it of the pattern "فَعْلاء"; this does not seem likely. In the speech of the Arabs it is "ناقَةٌ دَكّاءُ", i.e. having no hump. And "الجبل" (the mountain) is masculine, unless it is "جَعَلَهُ مِثْلَ دَكّاءَ" (He made it like a humpless one) with "مِثْل" omitted.

akhfash:148-148.t:
He said: ﴿مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ﴾, and some read ﴿حِلِيِّهِم﴾ and ﴿حَلْيِهِم﴾; ﴿عِجْلاً جَسَداً لَّهُ خُوَارٌ﴾, and some read ﴿جُوْارٌ﴾; and all are among the dialects of the Arabs.
As for His words ﴿مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ﴾ with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, it is "فُعول", the plural of "الحَلْيِ"; and whoever says ﴿حِلِيِّهِم﴾ in the other dialect does so on account of the yāʾ, just as they said "قِسِيّ" (bows) and "عِصِيّ" (sticks).

akhfash:149-149.t: He said: ﴿وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فَيۤ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾, and some read ﴿سَقَطَ﴾; all are permissible. The Arabs say "سُقِطَ في يديه" (he was filled with regret) and ﴿أُسْقِطَ في أيْدِيهِم﴾.

akhfash:150-150.t:
He said: ﴿ٱبْنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلْقَوْمَ﴾. That is — and Allah knows best — because he made it a single noun, like their saying "ابْنَ عَمِّ أَقْبِلْ" (Son of my uncle, come here!); this is not to be used as a basis for analogy. Some read ﴿يا ابنَ أُمي لا تَأْخُذ﴾, which is the analogical form, but the written text (al-kitāb, the muṣḥaf) has no yāʾ in it, so that was disliked. The poet said [in the khafīf metre, and it is the two hundred and thirteenth poetic witness]:
يَا ابْنَ أُميّ وَلَوْ شَهِدْتُكَ إِذْ تَدْ * عَو تَمِيماً وَأَنْتَ غَيْرَ مُجابِ
(O son of my mother, if only I had witnessed you when you called on Tamīm and were not answered.)
Some read ﴿ياابْنَ أُمِّ﴾, making it follow the dialect of those who say "this is my boy who has come" [i.e. dropping the possessive yāʾ and keeping the kasra], "or he made it a single noun whose end is kasra-marked", like "خازِبازِ".
And He said ﴿وَكَادُواْ يَقْتُلُونَنِي﴾: two nūns are retained in it, one belonging to the verb and the other to the latent (implied) pronoun noun. [Translator's note: the second nūn is in fact the nūn al-wiqāya before the attached pronoun ي; the source says «للاسم المضمر».] It is retained in the verb only because it is nominative, and the nominative of the verb, when it is for the plural or the dual, is by retaining the nūn; except that the plural nūn has fatḥa and the dual nūn has kasra. He has said ﴿أَتَعِدَانِنِيۤ أَنْ أُخْرَجَ﴾. Assimilation (idghām) and concealment (ikhfāʾ) are also permissible in this.

akhfash:154-154.t:
He said: ﴿وَلَماَّ سَكَتَ عَن مُّوسَى ٱلْغَضَبُ﴾, and some read ﴿سَكَنَ﴾, except that it does not accord with the written text, so ﴿سَكَتَ﴾ is read; and both are of the speech of the Arabs.
And He said ﴿لِّلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾, just as He said ﴿إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ﴾: He joined the verb [to its object] with the lām. Some said it means ﴿مِنْ أَجْلِ رَبِّهِم يَرْهَبُون﴾ (they fear for the sake of their Lord).

akhfash:155-155.t:
He said: ﴿وَٱخْتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلاً﴾, i.e. "he chose from his people"; when "مِنْ" was removed, the verb governed [the noun directly]. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the fourteenth poetic witness]: [Translator's note: the numbering here (14th, 15th, 16th) is as written in the source, which elsewhere in this passage counts above two hundred.]
مِنا الذي اخْتِيرَ الرجال سَماحَةً * وَجْوداً إِذا هَبَّ الرِّياحُ الزَعازِعُ
(From us is the one chosen from among men for magnanimity and generosity when the violent winds blow.)
Another said [in the basīṭ metre, and it is the fifteenth poetic witness]:
أَمَرْتُكَ الخَيْرَ فافْعَلْ ما أُمِرْتَ بِهِ * فَقَدْ تَرَكْتُكَ ذا مالٍ وَذا نَشَبِ
(I commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded, for I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
And al-Nābigha said [in the kāmil metre, and it is the sixteenth poetic witness]:
نُبِّئْتُ زُرْعةَ وَالسفَاهَةُ كاسْمِها * يُهْدِي إِلَيَّ أَوَابِدَ الأشْعار
(I was told [about] Zurʿa — and folly is as its name — that he sends me wild, unruly verses.)

akhfash:156-156.t: He said: ﴿وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾, i.e. it encompasses everyone who enters into it and does not fall short of anyone who enters it; or it may mean the mercy that He has divided among the creatures, by which some of them show tenderness to others, even the tenderness of the beast towards its young.

akhfash:160-160.t: He said: ﴿ٱثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ أَسْبَاطاً﴾: He meant twelve groups, then informed that the groups are tribes (asbāṭ); He did not make the number apply to "the tribes" [as its tamyīz, specification].

akhfash:168-168.t: He said: ﴿مِّنْهُمُ ٱلصَّالِحُونَ وَمِنْهُمْ دُونَ ذٰلِكَ﴾; we know of no one who reads it other than with the accusative.

akhfash:169-169.t:
He said: ﴿فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ﴾. When you say "خَلَفُ سَوءٍ" (an evil successor) and "خَلَفُ صِدْقٍ" (a true successor), the two are the same. By "الخَلْفُ" one means only what comes after what has passed, whether it was a successor (khalaf) from it or not; what is meant by it is the generation that comes after a generation. And "الخَلَفُ" is that which is a replacement for what was before it, having taken its place and done its work. You say: "أَصَبْتُ مِنْكَ خَلَفا" (I have found in you a replacement).
And He said ﴿يَأْخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَـٰذَا ٱلأَدْنَىٰ﴾: He annexed "العَرَضَ" to "هذا" and explained "هذا" by "الأَدْنى". Everything is ʿarḍ (goods) except dirhams and dinars, which are ʿayn (cash); whatever is other than that is ʿarḍ. As for "العَرَضُ", it is everything that befalls you. You say: "قد عرض له بعدي عَرُضٌ", i.e. "a calamity and evil befell him after me". And you say: "هذا عُرْضَةٌ للشَرِّ" (this is exposed to evil) and "عُرْضَةٌ للخَيْر" (exposed to good); all this the Arabs say. He said ﴿وَلاَ تَجْعَلُواْ ٱللَّهَ عُرْضَةً لأَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾. And you say "أَعْرَضَ لكَ الخيرُ" and "عَرَضَ لكَ الخَيْرُ" (good presented itself to you). The poet said [in the kāmil metre, and it is the two hundred and seventeenth poetic witness]: [Translator's note: the previous witness in this passage was numbered the sixteenth; the numbering is as in the source.]
أَعْرِفَنَّكَ مُعْرِضاً لِرِماحِنَا * في جُفِّ تُغْلِبَ واردَ الأَمْرارِ
(Let me not find you exposing yourself to our spears among the throng of Taghlib, coming down to the bitter waters.)
And "العارِضُ" of clouds is what faces you; it is the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضاً﴾. As for "الحَبِيُّ", it is what comes from every direction. You say "خُذُوهْ من عُرْضِ الناس", i.e. from those of them nearest you; likewise "اضرب به عُرْضَ الحائط", i.e. the part of it nearest you. As for "العَرْضُ" (breadth) as against "الطول" (length), it is with sukūn. As for his words [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and eighteenth poetic witness]:
[لَهُنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ عادَةٌ قَدْ عَرَفْنَها] * إِذا عَرَضُوا الخَطِّيَّ فَوْقَ الكَوَاثِب
(They [the horses] have a habit with them that they know well: when they lay the Khaṭṭī spears crosswise over the withers.)
and "أعرضوا" — this is because of: عَرَضَ عَرْضاً. And "عَرَضْتُ عَلَيْهِ المَنْزِلَ عَرْضاً" (I offered him the dwelling) and "عَرَضَ لِيَ أَمْرٌ عَرْضاً" (a matter presented itself to me): this is its maṣdar. And "العَرَضُ من الخَيْرِ والشَرِّ": whatever ʿaraḍ of this world you obtain and benefit from, by which you mean good. And "عَرَضَ لك عَرَضُ سَوْءٍ" (an evil accident befell you).

akhfash:176-176.t: He said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّهُ أَخْلَدَ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾; we know of no one who says ﴿خَلَدَ﴾. His words ﴿أَخْلَدَ﴾ mean: he resorted to it.

akhfash:177-177.t: He said: ﴿سَآءَ مَثَلاً ٱلْقَوْمُ﴾: in wording He made "القومُ" (the people) the "المَثَل" (the likeness), but He meant "the likeness of the people", and omitted it, just as He said "وَاسْأَل القَرْيَةَ".

akhfash:179-179.t: He said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ﴾; you say "ذَرَأَ" "يَذْرأُ" "ذَرْءاً" (to create, multiply).

akhfash:180-180.t: He said: ﴿وَذَرُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ فِيۤ أَسْمَآئِهِ﴾, and some read ﴿يُلْحَدُونَ﴾, deriving it from "لَحَدَ" "يَلْحَدُ", which is a dialect. [Translator's note: the variant is printed as «يُلْحَدُونَ» in the source; from لَحَدَ يَلْحَدُ one would expect «يَلْحَدُونَ».] And He said in another place ﴿لِّسَانُ ٱلَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ﴾ and ﴿يَلْحَدُون﴾; they are two dialects, and ﴿يُلْحدُونَ﴾ is more frequent, and that is how we read; it is supported by ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ﴾.

akhfash:189-189.t: He said: ﴿حَمَلَتْ حَمْلاً خَفِيفاً﴾, because "الحَمْلَ" is what is in the belly and "الحِمْل" is what is on the back. And He said ﴿وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَهَا﴾. As for His words ﴿أَثْقَلَتْ﴾, he says: "she became heavy-laden", just as you say "أَتْمَرْنا", i.e. "we came to have dates", and "أَلْبَنَّا" [i.e. we came to have milk], and "أَعْشَبَتِ الأَرْضُ" (the land became grassy) and "أَكْمَأَتْ" (it produced truffles). Some read ﴿فَلَمّا أُثْقِلَتْ﴾.

akhfash:190-190.t: He said: ﴿جَعَلاَ لَهُ شُرَكَآءَ فِيمَآ آتَاهُمَا﴾, and some read ﴿شِرْكاً﴾, because "الشِرْكَ" is just "الشِرْكَةُ" (partnership); and according to whoever reads thus, it ought to have said "فَجَعلا لغيرِه شِرْكاً فيما آتاهما" (so they gave others than Him a share in what He gave them).

akhfash:201-201.t:
He said: ﴿إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِّنَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ﴾, and ﴿الطَيْفُ﴾ is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs. The poet said [in the mutaqārib metre, and it is the two hundred and nineteenth poetic witness]:
أَلا يَا لَقَوْمٍ لِطَيْفِ الخَيالِ * أَرَّقَ مِنْ نازِحٍ ذِي دَلالِ
(O people, behold the phantom of the dream-image that kept me awake, from a coy one far away!)
We read it ﴿طائِف﴾ because the generality of the Readers follow it.

akhfash:205-205.t: He said: ﴿بِٱلْغُدُوِّ وَٱلآصَالِ﴾; its explanation is "بالغَدَواَتِ" (in the mornings), just as you say "آتيك طلوعَ الشَمْسِ" (I will come to you at sunrise), i.e. at the time of sunrise, as He said ﴿بِٱلْعَشِيِّ وَٱلإِبْكَارِ﴾. It is like "آتيكَ في الصَّباحِ وبِالمَساءِ" (I will come to you in the morning and in the evening). As for ﴿الآصال﴾, its singular is "أَصيلٌ", like "الأَشْرار" whose singular is "الشَرِير", and "الأَيْمانُ" whose singular is "اليَمِينُ".

akhfash:2-2.t:
[He said] ﴿كِتَابٌ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
And He said ﴿فَلاَ يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِّنْهُ﴾ as a prohibition, as He said ﴿وَلاَ تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ﴾, i.e. "as for distress, let it not be in your breast", and "as for your eyes, let them not pass beyond them".

akhfash:6-6.t: And He said ﴿فَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾, meaning: [We shall surely ask] the people to whom [messengers] were sent and who were warned. ﴿وَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾.

akhfash:7-7.t: ﴿فَلَنَقُصَّنَّ﴾: He put in the nūn and the lām because His saying ﴿فَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ﴾ ﴿وَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ is [in the form of] an oath.

akhfash:10-10.t: And He said ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَايِشَ﴾: the yāʾ is without hamza. Some readers have pronounced it with hamza, and that is poor, because it is not additional [i.e. it is radical]. Only what is on the pattern "مَفاعِل" is pronounced with hamza when the yāʾ is additional in the singular, as are the alif and the wāw [in the singular] whose place the hamza takes, as in "مَدائِن" (cities), because it is "فَعايِل". Whoever takes "المدائِن" from "دان", "يَدِين" does not use hamza, because the yāʾ is then radical. As for "قَطائِع", "رسائِل", "عَجائزِ" and "كبائر", all of these have hamza, because the wāw of "عَجُوز" is additional — do you not see that you say "عجزَ"? — and the alif of "رسالة" is additional, [since] you say "أَرسلت" and its alif goes; and you say of "كبيرة": "كبرت", and its yāʾ goes. As for "مصايِب" (misfortunes), its origin was "مصاوب", because when the yāʾ's origin is wāw and it comes in a position where it must be vowelled, the wāw is changed in that position [into yāʾ] if the origin is from wāw; and when it was changed, it became as if it had been corrupted, until it became as if it were the additional yāʾ; therefore it was given hamza, though analogy did not require that it take hamza. And some people among the Arabs say "المصاوب", and that is the regular analogy.

akhfash:11-11.t: And He said ﴿ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ﴾, because "ثُمَّ" has the meaning of wāw. And it may be that its meaning is [We fashioned] ﴿لآدَم﴾ (Adam), as you say to a people "قَدْ ضَرَبْناكُم" (we have struck you) when you struck only their chief.

akhfash:12-12.t:
And He said ﴿مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ﴾; its meaning is: what prevented you from prostrating; and ﴿لا﴾ here is zāʾida (redundant). The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the two hundred and fourth shāhid]:
أَبى جُودُهُ "لا" البُخْل واستعجلتْ بِهِ * "نَعَمْ" مِنْ فَتىً لا يَمْنَع الجوعِ قاتلَه
(His generosity refused the "no" of stinginess, and "yes" hastened [to come] from a young man who does not withhold from hunger its killer [i.e. food].)
The Arabs explained it: his generosity refused stinginess*, and they made ﴿لا﴾ redundant here as padding, connecting the speech with it. Yūnus claimed that Abū ʿAmr used to put "البخل" in the genitive and not make "لا" a construct attached to it [Translator's note: as written; the sense rather requires that he made "لا" the first term of a construct with "البخل"]; he meant: his generosity refused the ﴿لا﴾ which is for stinginess, because ﴿لا﴾ may be [a word] of generosity or of stinginess: if someone said to him "withhold the due" or "do not give the poor", and he said "no", this would be generosity from him.

akhfash:16-16.t:
And He said ﴿لأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾, i.e. on (على) Your path; and as you say "تَوَجَّهَ مَكَّةَ" (he headed Mecca), i.e. to Mecca. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the two hundred and fifth shāhid]:
كَأَنِّيَ إِذْ أَسْعَى لأَظْفَرَ طائراً * معَ النَّجْم في جَوِّ السَّماءِ يَصُوبُ
(It is as though, when I strive to catch [her], [I strive for] a bird swooping with the star in the vault of the sky.)
He means: to catch a bird (بطائرٍ); he dropped the bāʾ. And like it is ﴿أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ﴾, meaning: [hastened] away from (عن) the command of your Lord.

akhfash:18-18.t:
And He said ﴿ٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا مَذْءُوماً مَّدْحُوراً ﴾, because it is from "الذَأم" (disgrace): you say "ذَأَمْتُه", so "هُوَ مَذْؤُومٌ". The other way is from "الذَمّ" (blame): "ذَمَمْتُه", so "هو مَذْمُومٌ". You say "ذَأَمْتُهُ", "ذَمَمْتُه" and "ذِمْتُه", all in one meaning; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "ذِمْتُهُ" is "الذَّيْم".
And He said ﴿وَلَّمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ﴾: the first lām is the lām of ibtidāʾ (inception) and the second is for the oath.

akhfash:20-20.t:
And He said ﴿فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَانُ﴾, and the meaning is: Satan whispered to (إلى) them. But the Arabs connect the verb with all these particles. Some of them say "غَرِضْتُ" in the sense of "I longed for him", and its explanation is: I grew weary of these [and turned] to him.
And He said ﴿إِلاَّ أَنْ تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ﴾, meaning: ﴿ما نَهاكُما إلاّ﴾ out of dislike ﴿أَن تَكُونَا﴾, as you say "إِيَاكَ أَنْ تَفْعَلَ" (beware of doing), i.e. out of dislike that you should do.

akhfash:22-22.t:
And He said ﴿وَطَفِقَا﴾, and some read ﴿وَطَفقَا﴾. Whoever says "طَفَقَ" says "يَطْفِقُ", and whoever says "طَفِقَ" says "يَطْفَقُ".
And He said ﴿يَخْصِفَانِ﴾: he takes it from "يَخْتَصِفانِ"; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād and became unvowelled, and the khāʾ remained unvowelled, so the khāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters. Some of them give the khāʾ fatḥa, transferring the vowel of the tāʾ to it. It is like His saying ﴿أَمَّن لاَّ يَهِدِّيۤ﴾; and some read ﴿يَهِدِّي الا ان يُهْدَى﴾.

akhfash:23-23.t: And He said ﴿وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْخَاسِرِينَ﴾: it is as though it is an oath — and Allah knows best — as if they said: "By Allah, we shall surely be among the losers if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us".

akhfash:26-26.t: And He said ﴿قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاساً يُوَارِي سَوْءَاتِكُمْ وَرِيشاً وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ ذٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ﴾: He put His saying ﴿وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوىٰ﴾ in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and placed its khabar (predicate) in His saying ﴿ذٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ﴾. Some put ﴿وَلِباسَ التّقْوى﴾ in the accusative. And some read ﴿وَرِيشاً﴾, and that is how we read it; both are good and their meaning is one. [Translator's note: the other reading was evidently «وَرِيَاشاً»; the text writes ﴿وَرِيشاً﴾ both times.]

akhfash:30-30.t: And He said ﴿وَفَرِيقاً حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلضَّلاَلَةُ﴾, making the verb masculine because of the separation [between it and its feminine subject], as He said ﴿لاَ يُؤْخَذُ مِنكُمْ فِدْيَةٌ﴾.

akhfash:35-35.t: And He said ﴿يَابَنِيۤ آدَمَ إِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنكُمْ يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِي فَمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ وَأَصْلَحَ فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: it was as if He said "then obey them".

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَلِجَ ٱلْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ ٱلْخِيَاطِ﴾, from "وَلَجَ", "يَلِجُ", "وُلُوجاً" (to enter).

akhfash:41-41.t: And He said ﴿لَهُمْ مِّن جَهَنَّمَ مِهَادٌ وَمِن فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٍ﴾. His saying (غَواشٍ) has kasra only because this shīn is in the position of the ʿayn of "فواعِل", so it has kasra. As for the position of its lām [final radical], it is the yāʾ; and the yāʾ and the wāw, when they come after a kasra in a position to be vowelled with nominative or genitive, become an unvowelled yāʾ in the nominative and genitive, and take fatḥa in the accusative. When they became an unvowelled yāʾ and the tanwīn, which is unvowelled, was added to it, the yāʾ went because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters.

akhfash:43-44.t:
And He said ﴿وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ﴾: it is what is in the breasts [i.e. rancour]; as for that with which the captive is fettered, it is "الغُلّ" (the shackle).
And He said ﴿ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ ٱلَّذِي هَدَانَا لِهَـٰذَا﴾, as He said ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَهْدِي لِلْحَقِّ﴾. The Arabs say "هوَ لا يَهتَدِي لهذا", i.e. he does not know it. You say "هَدَيْتُ العروسَ إِلى بَعْلِها" (I led the bride to her husband), and you also say "أَهْدَيْتُها إلَيْه" and "هُدِيَتْ لَهُ", and you say "أَهْدَيْتُ لَهُ هَدِيَّةً" (I gave him a gift). The Banū Tamīm say "هَدَيْت العروسَ إِلى زَوْجِها", taking it in the sense of "I guided her", and Qays say "أَهْدَيْتُها", treating her like a gift.
And He said ﴿وَنُودُوۤاْ أَن تِلْكُمُ ٱلْجَنَّةُ﴾ and ﴿أَن لَّعْنَةُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾, and He said in another place ﴿أَنِ ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ﴾ and ﴿أَن قَدْ وَجَدْنَا مَا وَعَدَنَا رَبُّنَا حَقّاً﴾. This is the heavy "أَنّ" lightened, with [the pronoun] implied in it; it is not right to take it as the light [أَنْ], because after it is a noun, and nouns do not follow the light one. The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the two hundred and sixth shāhid]:
فِيَ فِتْيَةٍ كَسُيوفِ الهِنْدِ قَدْ عَلِمُوا * أنْ هالِكٌ كُلُّ مَنْ يَخْفى وَينْتَعِل
(Among young men like Indian swords, who know that everyone who goes barefoot or shod is perishing.) [Translator's note: «يَخْفى» is evidently for «يَحْفى» "goes barefoot".]
And the poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the two hundred and seventh shāhid]:
أُكاشِرُهُ وَاَعْلَمُ أَنْ كِلانا * عَلَى ما سَاءَ صاحِبَهُ حَريصُ
(I grin at him, knowing that each of us is eager for what harms the other.)
Its meaning is: that (أَنْهُ) each of us. And ﴿أَن قَدْ وَجَدْنَا﴾ may be in the sense of "أي" (that is to say).

akhfash:50-50.t: And His saying ﴿أَنْ أَفِيضُواْ عَلَيْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ﴾ may be "أيْ أَفِيضوا" (that is: pour), or it may be the "أنْ" that governs verbs, because you say "غَاظَني أَنْ قامَ" (it angered me that he stood) and "غَاظَنِي أَنْ ذَهَب" (it angered me that he went), so it falls on [past] verbs even though it does not govern them. In the Book of Allah: ﴿وَٱنطَلَقَ ٱلْمَلأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ ٱمْشُواْ﴾, whose meaning is: that is, walk on.

akhfash:53-53.t: And He said ﴿فَهَل لَّنَا مِن شُفَعَآءَ فَيَشْفَعُواْ لَنَآ أَوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ غَيْرَ ٱلَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ﴾: He put what follows the fāʾ in the accusative because it is the answer to a question.
